//: Curated benchmark set for the nightly benchlab run. Each target is measured at three commits in one benchlab invocation, so the cost of adding a target is roughly three times its plain benchmark time -- see build/bench-nightly/main.go. Cost is per case and independent of how fast the case is, since -benchtime is fixed: one case is reps * benchtime * 3 arms. The full published set is ~1118 cases, far too many to measure this way nightly. A target without a "bench" selects its package's BenchmarkBenchlab* wrappers, defined in that package's benchlab_test.go, which is where the set is decided; the remaining regexes are held over until those packages grow one.

targets.//: Rule evaluation, comprehensions, bindings, partial eval, base-document access and iteration. Deliberately excludes the JSONPatch*, Tokens and Builtin* families, which are builtin micro-benchmarks rather than evaluation hot paths.
Parsing, object/set construction and lookup, and term rewriting. Excludes the NoASTTypeAllocates*/NoNodeTypeAllocates* families, which are allocation assertions rather than trend material.
All ~53 cases: the public evaluation API, the closest thing here to end-to-end user-visible performance.
All ~48 cases: the store read/write hot path.
opa build over increasingly many dynamically-selected policies, and against large partial rule sets. Both families exist because of filed regressions (#5216, #5756).
Any.Merge/Union, reached from types.Or on the type checker's hot path, plus Type.Select.
opa fmt / LSP formatting of a large policy.
WASM eval, the Rego-to-WASM compiler, and a Go arm to compare against. Requires the opa_wasm build tag, which is already the default.
The coverage tracer's overhead, paid by every opa test --coverage run.
The profiler's overhead, on the same shapes as v1/cover so the two are comparable.
A comprehension-heavy Kubernetes policy, compiled and evaluated per iteration.
opa deps. The lowest-value target in this shard; cut first if the shard needs to shrink.
